chapter: After the Army: JATP, clubs and first Europe trips
title: Bebop musicians ignoring the audience
summary: They agree that turning one's back and not announcing numbers was rude behavior after bop.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well then you know, there was the, after bop had become popular, there was the business where they ignored the audience totally.
Turned their backs towards them. Now I mean, that's another kind of rudeness in my point of view.
Oh very rude, yes. In other words, you are lucky to be there. You are lucky to listen to me play. No matter if I turn my back on you, that's the attitude they used to have.

reverse of the person, the people in the audience that talk so loudly and that's rude. But the idea that you can turn your back to the audience and not announce the numbers and not acknowledge applause.
Well that's part of the revolution.
